items.title: Bob Magnusson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: I used to work there a lot with Frank Rosolino and Joe Diorio and all kinds of different people.

ctx.x: Really. What was this Road Work Ahead?

Road Work Ahead that’s a funny story because the record I just mentioned that I did with Joe Farrell, I had Bill Mays, who I had been friends with for years, knew him from San Diego, played piano, John Guerin played drums. I played with a wonderful drummer and percussionist in San Diego, Jim Plank, he played percussion on it. And Albert Marks, if you remember Albert Marks, he had Discovery Records and Trend Records. He was the producer of this record I did. Well the record came out and they were playing it on the…

Charles MacPherson and a lot of different, great people. Peter was in San Diego, and Jim Plank. So we put that group together. And we called it the Bob Magnusson Quartet and we started playing. And we were all having such a great time together with the group, and everybody was kind of writing and contributing music, and Bill was making arrangement. Bill is a prolific writer and wonderful, and Peter is too. And Peter would get us jobs in San Diego and we’d call it the Peter Sprague Quartet, and Bill would get a…
